## Food-System Buffer Monitoring & Anticipatory Decision-Making

<p class="eyebrow">Developing research direction · Submitted CPRA proposal</p>

The developing work asks how stress signals and weakening food-system buffers can be identified early enough to inform adaptation and policy. The CPRA proposal has been submitted; it is not an awarded or funded fellowship.

<div class="framework"><ol class="framework-stages"><li><span class="step-number" aria-hidden="true">01</span><h3>Stress signals</h3><p>Environmental · Remote sensing · Market · Socio-economic · Political-institutional</p></li><li><span class="step-number" aria-hidden="true">02</span><h3>Food-system buffers</h3><p>Environmental · Market · Livelihood · Institutional · Social-political</p></li><li><span class="step-number" aria-hidden="true">03</span><h3>Situation update</h3><p>What stress is increasing? Which buffers are weakening? What remains available? Who can access it?</p></li><li><span class="step-number" aria-hidden="true">04</span><h3>Anticipatory decision</h3><p>What adaptation or policy response is still possible?</p></li></ol></div>

The proposed work is designed to engage networks connected through Arrell Food Institute and Professor Evan Fraser, including FAO, Oxford Martin School, Cornell, and the RAAPID Center (University of Maryland/NASA Harvest). These are prospective network connections for the developing work.

## Place-based research interest: Bangladesh

Bangladesh has been a long-term research and professional context for my work on water quality, environmental risk, climate adaptation, agricultural resilience, and science–policy practice. I am interested in future collaborations connecting this experience with Earth observation, GeoAI, agricultural landscape management, and food-system resilience, including comparative work between Canada and Bangladesh.
